hints: Use index laws to collect all expressions raised to the power $x$ before taking logarithms.
Rewrite $2^{3x-1}=5\cdot3^{-x}$ by clearing the factor $2^{-1}$ and combining $2^{3x}$ with $3^x$.
Once the equation has the form $b^x=a$, take natural logarithms and isolate $x$ in the requested $\ln a/\ln b$ form.
walkthrough:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides of the equation $2^{3x - 1} = 5(3^{-x})$:
$$\ln\left(2^{3x - 1}\right) = \ln\left(5 \times 3^{-x}\right)$$

Apply the power and product laws of logarithms:
$$(3x - 1)\ln 2 = \ln 5 + \ln\left(3^{-x}\right)$$
$$(3x - 1)\ln 2 = \ln 5 - x\ln 3$$

Collect terms containing $x$ on the left-hand side and constants on the right-hand side:
$$3x\ln 2 + x\ln 3 = \ln 5 + \ln 2$$
$$x(3\ln 2 + \ln 3) = \ln 5 + \ln 2$$

Simplify the logarithmic expressions using laws of logarithms:
$$3\ln 2 = \ln\left(2^3\right) = \ln 8$$
$$3\ln 2 + \ln 3 = \ln 8 + \ln 3 = \ln(8 \times 3) = \ln 24$$
$$\ln 5 + \ln 2 = \ln(5 \times 2) = \ln 10$$

Substitute these simplified expressions back into the equation:
$$x\ln 24 = \ln 10$$

Divide by $\ln 24$ to isolate $x$ in the required form $\dfrac{\ln a}{\ln b}$ with integers $a = 10$ and $b = 24$:
$$x = \dfrac{\ln 10}{\ln 24}$$
